A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BBox-Mask-Pose research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary materials are readable and support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original COCO and OCHuman evaluations, component ablations, extensive SAM prompting experiments and qualitative failure analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results, revises reported outcomes, and adds measured runtime results and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The detector–MaskPose–SAM loop, masking procedure and keypoint selection algorithm are retained. However, Section 3.2 changes the stated MaskPose output count from 21 to 22 keypoints without explaining whether the implemented head changed or the earlier count was incorrect. The added equations alone do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 narrows the reported detector fine-tuning coverage from COCO covering all 80 classes to COCO-human. Pose training still uses COCO, AIC and MPII, and evaluation retains COCO, OCHuman and the same three human-body tasks. No additional benchmark or distinct test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially broadens comparison beyond the original three detectors, adding HQNet R-50, CoDETR SWIN-L, Occlusion C&P, ExPoSeg and Crowd-SAM. Table 1 also adds HQNet R-50 for pose estimation. These are reported comparisons, including segmentation-specific competitors previously absent from the evaluation.

E3.justification: The reported detector fine-tuning setting changes from all-class COCO to COCO-human. V2 introduces timed evaluation on an A100 40 GB GPU and identifies HQNet's exclusion of small COCO instances. Epoch budgets and NMS thresholds remain unchanged. These reported settings do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a measured runtime-versus-accuracy analysis in Table 5 and additional qualitative comparisons in Figures 12–13. The component ablations and extensive appendix SAM prompting and failure analyses are retained. Appendix Table 9 redisplays v1 Table 4's parameter-count results rather than adding a new ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Both present point estimates; keypoint confidence thresholds concern model predictions rather than uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Reported OCHuman-test BMP 2× pose AP changes from 48.2 to 49.2, overtaking the retained BUCTD 2× score of 48.3. Its detection/mask AP changes from 31.3/32.4 to 35.9/34.0; BMP 1× mask AP decreases from 31.1 to 30.2. COCO scores also change, including CID-w48 from 69.8 to 68.9. V2 removes Table 1's validation column, replaces overlap-bin results, and adds comparator and runtime entries. Revised training documentation and unreconciled results prevent treating these uniformly as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The added equations express the already-described masking, conditioning, SAM calls and iterative loop. The existing pose-mask consistency formula is retained as Equation 6. No new theorem, proof, substantive derivation or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion strengthen the central claim from matching leading pose-estimation performance to setting new OCHuman state of the art in all three tasks. V2 adds a 39% detection-improvement claim for overlapping instances and makes faster, smaller specialized models versus foundational models a central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 interprets measured runtimes as support for specialized models over large foundational models and adds the unsuccessful attempt to train a reliable visibility predictor. It removes the unverified low-light limitation and the explanation that parameter-count complexity ignores per-instance processing. Most SAM failure mechanisms and applicability limitations remain unchanged, including Appendices A–B.

D1.justification: V2 discloses timing hardware, explicitly requires retraining for a chosen masking transparency, and explains that overlap-bin evaluation partitions ground truth while leaving detections unsplit. It revises the stated keypoint count to 22 and notes unavailable HQNet ViT-L weights. V1's random-patch masking detail is omitted. The SAM version, post-processing settings, epoch counts and project link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Crowd-SAM, HQNet and Occlusion Copy & Paste, and brings previously cited Co-DETR and PoSeg/ExPoSeg into explicit comparisons. It emphasizes competition with unified and foundational approaches while retaining the established positioning around mutual conditioning and mask-conditioned pose estimation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusions undergo substantial rewriting. Related work gains thematic labels, conditioning is explained through explicit functional notation, overlap analysis moves within the results narrative, and parameter-count discussion is partly relocated to the new Appendix C.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with clearer instance colors and combined outputs. Tables 1, 2 and 4 change structure; runtime Table 5 and qualitative Figures 12–13 are added. Parameter counts reappear in appendix Table 9, Figure 3 moves, and Figures 10–11 exchange numbering and placement. Most existing figures and appendix tables retain their design.

improvement.justification: V2 improves comparison breadth, adds measured efficiency evidence and clarifies conditioning. However, its revised results introduce unresolved inconsistencies: Section 4.2 still calls MaskPose and BMP 1× identical despite Table 1 reporting 45.0 versus 46.6 AP. Table 3 reports BMP 2× OCHuman-val detection AP of 35.7, while Tables 4 and 9 retain 32.1 without explaining different settings. V1's corresponding results agreed. These reliability problems counterbalance the added evidence, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
